deck.title: Energy Levels in Atoms & Line Spectra

front_blocks.md: Define the **ground state**.

back_blocks.md: The **ground state** is the lowest energy level normally occupied by an electron in an atom.

cards.front_md: Define the **ground state**.
cards.back_md: The **ground state** is the lowest energy level normally occupied by an electron in an atom.

front_blocks.md: Define **excitation**.

back_blocks.md: **Excitation** is the process in which an electron gains energy and moves up to a higher energy level, becoming an **excited state** electron.

cards.front_md: Define **excitation**.
cards.back_md: **Excitation** is the process in which an electron gains energy and moves up to a higher energy level, becoming an **excited state** electron.

front_blocks.md: Define **ionisation**.

back_blocks.md: **Ionisation** occurs when an electron gains enough energy to be removed from the atom entirely.

cards.front_md: Define **ionisation**.
cards.back_md: **Ionisation** occurs when an electron gains enough energy to be removed from the atom entirely.

front_blocks.md: State three ways an electron can absorb energy in order to move to a higher energy level.

back_blocks.md:
- Collisions with other atoms or electrons
- Absorbing a photon
- A physical source, such as heat

cards.front_md: State three ways an electron can absorb energy in order to move to a higher energy level.
cards.back_md:
- Collisions with other atoms or electrons
- Absorbing a photon
- A physical source, such as heat

front_blocks.md: What happens when an electron returns to a lower energy level from a higher, excited state?

back_blocks.md: It releases energy in the form of a **photon**.

cards.front_md: What happens when an electron returns to a lower energy level from a higher, excited state?
cards.back_md: It releases energy in the form of a **photon**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Electrons in an atom can have any value of energy.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Electrons in an atom can only have certain specific, **discrete** energies, called electron energy levels.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Electrons in an atom can have any value of energy.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Electrons in an atom can only have certain specific, **discrete** energies, called electron energy levels.

front_blocks.md: Define **line spectra**.

back_blocks.md: **Line spectra** are a series of coloured lines with dark spaces in between, produced when excited atoms emit light of certain wavelengths.

cards.front_md: Define **line spectra**.
cards.back_md: **Line spectra** are a series of coloured lines with dark spaces in between, produced when excited atoms emit light of certain wavelengths.

front_blocks.md: Why can elements be identified using their line spectrum?

back_blocks.md: Each element produces a **unique** set of spectral lines — no two elements emit the same set.

cards.front_md: Why can elements be identified using their line spectrum?
cards.back_md: Each element produces a **unique** set of spectral lines — no two elements emit the same set.

front_blocks.md: Define an **emission spectrum**.

back_blocks.md: An **emission spectrum** is a set of discrete wavelengths, seen as coloured lines on a black background, produced when electrons transition from a higher to a lower energy level, emitting photons.

cards.front_md: Define an **emission spectrum**.
cards.back_md: An **emission spectrum** is a set of discrete wavelengths, seen as coloured lines on a black background, produced when electrons transition from a higher to a lower energy level, emitting photons.

front_blocks.md: Define an **absorption spectrum**.

back_blocks.md: An **absorption spectrum** is a continuous spectrum with dark lines at certain wavelengths, produced when a cool, low-pressure gas absorbs certain wavelengths from white light passing through it.

cards.front_md: Define an **absorption spectrum**.
cards.back_md: An **absorption spectrum** is a continuous spectrum with dark lines at certain wavelengths, produced when a cool, low-pressure gas absorbs certain wavelengths from white light passing through it.

front_blocks.md: State the equation relating the energy change Δ*E* of an electron transition to the wavelength *λ* of the photon emitted or absorbed.

back_blocks.md: $Δ E = h f = \frac{hc}{λ}$

cards.front_md: State the equation relating the energy change Δ*E* of an electron transition to the wavelength *λ* of the photon emitted or absorbed.
cards.back_md: $Δ E = h f = \frac{hc}{λ}$

front_blocks.md: Why do certain wavelengths appear to be missing from an absorption spectrum, rather than simply absent?

back_blocks.md: Absorbed photons are re-emitted as electrons return to lower energy levels, but in **all directions** rather than the original direction of the white light, so those wavelengths appear missing from the transmitted beam.

cards.front_md: Why do certain wavelengths appear to be missing from an absorption spectrum, rather than simply absent?
cards.back_md: Absorbed photons are re-emitted as electrons return to lower energy levels, but in **all directions** rather than the original direction of the white light, so those wavelengths appear missing from the transmitted beam.

front_blocks.md: The wavelengths missing from an absorption spectrum are the **..........** as their corresponding emission spectrum of the same element.

back_blocks.md: The wavelengths missing from an absorption spectrum are the **same** as their corresponding emission spectrum of the same element.

cards.front_md: The wavelengths missing from an absorption spectrum are the **..........** as their corresponding emission spectrum of the same element.
cards.back_md: The wavelengths missing from an absorption spectrum are the **same** as their corresponding emission spectrum of the same element.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An absorption spectrum is produced by passing white light through a hot, high-pressure gas.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
An absorption spectrum is produced by passing white light through a **cool, low-pressure** gas.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

cards.back_md:

An absorption spectrum is produced by passing white light through a **cool, low-pressure** gas.

front_blocks.md: In the equation Δ*E* = *E*<sub>2</sub> − *E*<sub>1</sub>, which energy level is *E*<sub>1</sub> and which is *E*<sub>2</sub>?

back_blocks.md: *E*<sub>1</sub> is the energy of the **lower** level; *E*<sub>2</sub> is the energy of the **higher** level.

front_blocks.md: How do you convert an energy value from eV into joules?

back_blocks.md: **Multiply** the value in eV by 1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup>.

cards.front_md: How do you convert an energy value from eV into joules?

front_blocks.md: The difference between two energy levels is equal to a specific **..........** energy.

back_blocks.md: The difference between two energy levels is equal to a specific **photon** energy.

cards.front_md: The difference between two energy levels is equal to a specific **..........** energy.
cards.back_md: The difference between two energy levels is equal to a specific **photon** energy.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The largest energy change between two levels corresponds to the longest wavelength of radiation emitted.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Wavelength and photon energy are inversely proportional, so the **largest** energy change corresponds to the **shortest** wavelength.
